teaser.text: AT&T sells access: the connections that let people, businesses and public agencies call, message and use the internet. Its business becomes clearer when we follow those connections from the products AT&T sells to the customers who pay for them and the costs that consume each dollar.

stock.title: AT&T stock forecast
stock.meta_description: AT&T's stock forecast weighs the $21.93 weighted price in October 2027 against cash generation, debt, network investment and competition.
stock.opening: AT&T's weighted forecast is $21.93 in October 2027, rising to $30.52 in October 2029. AT&T's outcome hinges on turning network investment into profitable growth while reducing debt.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains AT&T's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could AT&T's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast assigns 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to base and 20% to bull. The September-quarter report on October 21, 2026, should show EchoStar’s effect on debt, cash, investment and customers. Fiber additions, wireless service growth, the expected Q1 2027 Mexico sale and fiber-venture proceeds are key catalysts. Debt reduction toward 2.5 times and most copper shutdowns are targeted around 2029.

The forecast points to limited first-year appreciation but meaningful potential by October 2029. The weighted price is $21.93 in October 2027, a 1% total return including dividends. It rises to $25.63 in October 2028, a 22% return, and reaches $30.52 in October 2029, a 48% return.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for AT&T?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls to $45,751 million by the final date because legacy losses, competition and delayed cost removal overwhelm growth. The bull case reaches $55,151 million because fiber take-up, wireless economics and deployed spectrum produce faster connectivity growth. Fiber added 367,000 customers in the June quarter, while wireless service revenue grew 3.3%.

blocks.heading: How much cash does AT&T really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations was $40,284 million in 2025. After capital spending of $21,221 million, free cash flow was $19,063 million. Deducting $536 million of stock compensation produces $18,527 million of “real free cash flow,” treating shares issued to employees as an economic cost to owners.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for AT&T today?

paragraphs.text: At $22.86 on October 13, 2026, one share buys a small ownership interest in AT&T’s wireless and broadband operations. All its shares together are worth $156,645.54 million. Enterprise value, which includes the debt a buyer would inherit, is $283,029.54 million. At June 30, AT&T had $144.0 billion of debt and $17.6 billion of cash. Its net debt was therefore $126.4 billion, like a mortgage sitting above the owners’ stake.

blocks.heading: How much does AT&T pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: The WarnerMedia separation changed the dividend promise. AT&T reset its annual common dividend from $2.08 to $1.11 per share so the remaining communications business could fund fiber and wireless investment. Dividends paid fell from $15,068 million in 2021 to $8,180 million in 2025.

blocks.heading: Does AT&T’s dividend come from cash it makes?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, free cash flow reached $19.063 billion, while buybacks reached $4.5 billion. A buyback retires shares, giving the remaining shares a larger claim on future earnings, but it does not by itself repay acquisition debt. AT&T’s latest plan puts approximately $18 billion of dividends and buybacks against its 2026 free-cash-flow outlook, leaving less room for acquisitions or debt reduction.

blocks.heading: What is AT&T’s dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: At $22.86 on October 13, 2026, one share buys a small ownership interest in AT&T’s wireless and broadband operations. All its shares together are worth $156,645.54 million. Enterprise value, which includes the debt a buyer would inherit, is $283,029.54 million. At June 30, AT&T had $144.0 billion of debt and $17.6 billion of cash. Its net debt was therefore $126.4 billion, like a mortgage sitting above the owners’ stake.
The 4.9% dividend yield is attractive, but dividends and buybacks together appear to use roughly the planned free cash flow. Debt reduction therefore depends on cash left after every claim.

blocks.heading: What has AT&T guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: AT&T’s starting point is service revenue: the monthly bills customers pay for mobile service and home internet, excluding equipment sales. Management expects that revenue to grow in the low single digits through 2028. Advanced Connectivity, which contains modern wireless and fiber services, should grow faster, while the old copper business shrinks. AT&T is therefore replacing one source of income with another.

blocks.heading: Has AT&T kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: AT&T also has evidence of keeping promises. It forecast at least $16 billion of 2025 free cash flow excluding DIRECTV and later reported $16.6 billion on that basis. New tax provisions improved cash generation, so the result cannot all be credited to stronger operations. Management also brought forward planned repurchases, which returns money faster but does not necessarily increase the total commitment.

blocks.heading: What do AT&T's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The eight-quarter sequence includes unusually weak and strong quarters, so June cannot establish a trend by itself. Its customer and service measures support improvement; its tax benefit and depreciation change require separate treatment.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in AT&T's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next checkpoint is the October 21, 2026 quarterly report. Its September balance sheet should show the effect of the EchoStar closing. Investors can then compare cash, borrowing, repurchases and investment with customer growth and service revenue. Discounted bundles may lower fiber ARPU, or average revenue per user, so the question is whether each household relationship lasts long enough to repay the discount.

The network milestones also need interpretation. AT&T targets 40 million fiber locations and 70% of wireless traffic on open-capable platforms by year-end 2026. A location reached is not necessarily a subscriber, and open-capable equipment is not the same as a fully interchangeable network. Take-up matters: industry averages were 40% of homes passed, or 46.5% when measured against unique passings.
